questions.cardText:
[Economics] What is Keynesian economics?
A. It states that government intervention is necessary to stabilize economies
B. It advocates for minimal government intervention in the economy
C. It focuses on long-term growth at the expense of short-term loss of wages
Answer: A. John Maynard Keynes’ ideas were so influential that they led to the establishment of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
questions.de: Was ist nach der keynesianischen Wirtschaftslehre nötig, um Volkswirtschaften etwa in Rezessionen zu stabilisieren?
questions.en: According to Keynesian economics, what is needed to stabilize economies, for example during recessions?

timeline.labelEn: Keynes publishes The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, the basis of Keynesian economics
timeline.labelDe: Keynes veröffentlicht „Allgemeine Theorie der Beschäftigung, des Zinses und des Geldes“, die Grundlage des Keynesianismus

questions.notes: Wikipedia: Keynesians advocate an active role for government intervention during recessions and depressions. The explanation's IMF/World Bank claim is loose: Keynes led the British delegation at the 1944 Bretton Woods conference that created both institutions (they were not founded on Keynesian theory as such).

questions.cardText:
[Art History] What is a “macguffin” in a film?
A. An object that triggers the plot but has no other purpose
B. A type of camera angle
C. The nadir of the plot
Answer: A.
questions.de: Wie nennt man in einem Film ein Objekt, das die Handlung in Gang setzt, aber sonst keine Bedeutung hat – ein von Alfred Hitchcock populär gemachter Begriff?
questions.en: What is the term, popularized by Alfred Hitchcock, for an object in a film that sets the plot in motion but has no other significance?

timeline.labelEn: Alfred Hitchcock popularizes the MacGuffin with his film The 39 Steps
timeline.labelDe: Alfred Hitchcock macht den MacGuffin mit seinem Film „Die 39 Stufen“ populär

questions.notes: Card spells it 'macguffin'; standard spelling MacGuffin. Term originated by Angus MacPhail, popularized by Hitchcock (Wikipedia). Discipline label 'Art History' is the card's own.
